storyboard.claim: Her family-priority line exposes her immaturity and control tactics, not your cruelty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Neighbor smirks and points a guilt line while Everyman weighs it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the section on guilt-trip pressure from relatives.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk plus pointing shows pressure aimed at you.

storyboard.claim: Taking on someone else's tantrum makes you hostage to whoever cries or pouts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped under chains, bound by other people's moods.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the point that you cannot manage other adults' emotions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as bound and controlled, which is the literal claim of being held hostage.

storyboard.claim: Triggering an emotion is not the same as causing it; the distinction is important.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman studying an emotion under a magnifier.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the triggering-versus-causing distinction from the previous beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: Magnifier shows the distinction being examined.

storyboard.claim: A tearful person in the lobby does not oblige you to open your savings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Neighbor tearful while Everyman keeps the wallet closed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the bank-account metaphor from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sad neighbor beside a guarded wallet separates distress from obligation.

storyboard.claim: The strongest pressure to say yes often comes from inside, not from other people.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman alone, worried, pressure coming from inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from outside pressure to internal pressure.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no outside person on screen is the point; callout names the source.

callout.text: Ego and fear of missing out

storyboard.claim: The yes-pressure comes from our own ego and fear of missing out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman afraid, gripping a phone full of invitations.
storyboard.onScreenText: Ego and fear of missing out
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the inside-pressure point from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Phone in hand shows the missing-out fear.

storyboard.claim: A prestigious committee invitation is an ego-driven trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman, pleased, holding a trophy: the prize that lures.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the prestige example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy reads as status and a prize, the literal lure of prestige.

storyboard.claim: You are already overloaded with tasks before the invitation arrives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped holding an overfull task list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the existing workload against the flattering offer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Full notes make the workload literal.

storyboard.claim: Your inbox is a disaster and you are short on sleep, yet the prestige still tempts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding a phone, the inbox overloaded.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the overload behind the tempting email.
storyboard.addedInformation: Phone reads as the modern inbox the narration describes.

callout.text: Will I miss my big break?

storyboard.claim: Fear of missing a big break makes the refusal feel impossible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman afraid, staring at the invitation on his phone.
storyboard.onScreenText: Will I miss my big break?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the inner question that drives the decision.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fear is on the face and in the narrator's question.

storyboard.claim: Case-by-case decisions let ego and FOMO win, because every yes can be justified.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman smirking, clutching a trophy as ego justifies yes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the danger of deciding one request at a time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk plus trophy shows ego winning.

storyboard.claim: You convince yourself this one opportunity is the exception, and then you drown.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman smirks, convincing himself with a bright idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the self-talk that leads to a yes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk shows the self-persuasion.

storyboard.claim: A blanket rule removes the decision from the heat of the moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing at a shield: the blanket rule as protection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Offers the blanket rule as the fix.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield reads as protection, the literal function of a blanket rule.

storyboard.claim: Zahariades recommends defining a deal-breaking attribute before requests arrive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing at a written rule list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the strategy named in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing at the list shows the rule being defined.

storyboard.claim: Sorting requests into categories replaces agonizing over each one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman, a lightbulb: the idea of a rule to sort requests.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the strategy works.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lightbulb reads as an idea, the literal moment of inventing a rule.

storyboard.claim: Auto-reject any request that takes more than thirty minutes of your time per week.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing, a clock marking the thirty-minute limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the concrete hard rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clock reads as time, the literal limit on the rule.

storyboard.claim: You reject the category of time-intensive requests, not the individual opportunity, so the refusal feels less personal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman calmly turning down a friend's request by rule.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the rule depersonalises the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Friend as requester makes the impersonal refusal visible.

storyboard.claim: Does a blanket rule make you a rigid, unadaptable robot?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman with a blank, robotic stare.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the objection to the blanket rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank face carries the robot objection.

storyboard.claim: A blanket rule may cause you to miss spontaneous opportunities.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman, afraid, a door standing closed in front of them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Presents the objection about missing opportunities.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door reads as a way in or out, the closed door of a missed chance.

storyboard.claim: Missing a few opportunities is the unavoidable cost of having boundaries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman sadly accepting a lost chance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the objection with the trade-off.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sad face shows the cost being paid.

storyboard.claim: The rule saves you from most spontaneous misery, a good trade-off.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman celebrating relief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the benefit that outweighs the cost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Celebrate shows the benefit outweighing the cost.

storyboard.claim: A spontaneous opportunity is usually a pile of extra uncompensated work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped under a stack of notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the romantic idea of opportunity as work.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stacked notes make the pile literal.

callout.text: Work that someone else didn't want

storyboard.claim: Spontaneous opportunities are often work that someone else did not want to do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss pointing at Everyman and handing over a stack of notes.
storyboard.onScreenText: Work that someone else didn't want
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the pile-of-work point.
storyboard.addedInformation: Boss first so the task-dropping reads as the subject of the sentence.

storyboard.claim: Without a baseline, other people's priorities take control of your time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman, worried, a puppeteer controlling them from above.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the cost of having no baseline rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer reads as one person controlling others, the literal claim.

storyboard.claim: A categorical rule works like an automatic block on costly transactions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: categorical rejection leads to an automatic block on costly withdrawals.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the bank analogy for the blanket rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: The diagram draws the analogy the narrator describes.

storyboard.claim: The automatic block bounces requests without you having to think.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman, relieved, at ease.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the bank analogy with its benefit.
storyboard.addedInformation: Happy reads as relief at no longer deciding each request.

storyboard.claim: Saying no to a boss, an aunt, or rigid rules can feel frightening.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman cowering before the boss.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the fear that makes boundaries hard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Boss in frame names whom the refusal frightens.

storyboard.claim: You build the no muscle gradually; you do not start with the hardest refusal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman eyeing the boss as the hardest refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the step-by-step training idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: Boss stands in for the final-boss refusal.

storyboard.claim: Begin with a scene where nothing is at stake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman relaxed in a casual setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the retail checkout example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Relaxed cafe face shows nothing at stake.

storyboard.claim: You are at a clothing store checkout buying socks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding a wallet at a shop counter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the checkout scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Wallet places the small purchase.

storyboard.claim: The clerk offers a store credit card to save fifteen percent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Friend as clerk pitching a card to Everyman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Presents the sales pitch.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pitching friend is the sales offer.

storyboard.claim: You want the discount but know you should not open another credit card.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman torn, wallet in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the internal conflict at the counter.
storyboard.addedInformation: Wallet shows the card temptation.

storyboard.claim: A low-stakes moment is a free training ground for assertiveness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman celebrating a gift, the free practice moment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the checkout as practice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gift reads as something given freely, the literal opportunity.

storyboard.claim: Practise saying no in easy cases such as a barista offering a pastry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding a coffee, waving off a pastry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the easy wins to practise.
storyboard.addedInformation: Cup and cafe place the barista.

storyboard.claim: Retail staff hear refusals hundreds of times a day and will not take offence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Friend as clerk smiling, unbothered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reassures the listener about easy refusals.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smiling clerk shows no offence.

storyboard.claim: Easy refusals build confidence, but their translation to harder cases is limited.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman talking, a lightbulb of insight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the value of practice and its limit.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the claim about transfer is carried by the narration; the callout names the benefit.

storyboard.claim: Refusing a stranger is a different experience from refusing your spouse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A split frame: Everyman thinking beside a second figure, two different stakes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the stranger with a close relationship.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the spouse is not on screen; the second figure stands in for the contrast.

storyboard.claim: Practising with a sock salesman does not prepare you for a marital boundary directly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman doubting, a tougher opponent beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the doubt about direct transfer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Second figure implies higher stakes.

storyboard.claim: Assertiveness grows with repetition, the way a muscle does.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman celebrating a small win.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the doubt with the muscle analogy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Celebration shows growth through repetition.

storyboard.claim: Starting too heavy crushes you and ends the practice; begin with the empty bar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped, crushed by starting too heavy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the gym analogy with the advice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump shows the cost of starting heavy.
